# src/actor/actor.rs

```rust
use std::any::TypeId;

use slotmap::new_key_type;
use thiserror::Error;

use crate::graphics::RenderNode;

use super::context::ActorContext;
use super::message::Message;

new_key_type! {
    /// Unique identifier for an actor in the system.
    /// Uses slotmap for efficient O(1) lookup and generation tracking.
    pub struct ActorId;
}

/// Errors that can occur during message handling.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Error)]
pub enum ActorError {
    /// The message type is not supported by this actor.
    #[error("unsupported message type: {0}")]
    UnsupportedMessage(String),

    /// An internal error occurred during processing.
    #[error("internal error: {0}")]
    Internal(String),

    /// A required resource was not found.
    #[error("resource not found: {0}")]
    ResourceNotFound(String),

    /// The actor is in an invalid state for this operation.
    #[error("invalid state: {0}")]
    InvalidState(String),

    /// A child actor reported an error (for supervision).
    #[error("child actor {actor:?} failed: {error}")]
    ChildError {
        actor: ActorId,
        error: Box<ActorError>,
    },
}

/// Result of handling a message.
#[must_use = "handle result indicates success/failure and should be checked"]
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum HandleResult {
    /// Message was handled successfully.
    Handled,
    /// Message was not handled (actor doesn't handle this type).
    NotHandled,
    /// Message handling failed with an error.
    Error(ActorError),
}

impl HandleResult {
    /// Create an error result from a string message.
    pub fn error(msg: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::Error(ActorError::Internal(msg.into()))
    }

    /// Check if the result is an error.
    pub fn is_error(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::Error(_))
    }

    /// Check if the message was handled (either success or error).
    pub fn was_handled(&self) -> bool {
        !matches!(self, Self::NotHandled)
    }
}

impl PartialEq for HandleResult {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        match (self, other) {
            (HandleResult::Handled, HandleResult::Handled) => true,
            (HandleResult::NotHandled, HandleResult::NotHandled) => true,
            (HandleResult::Error(e1), HandleResult::Error(e2)) => e1.to_string() == e2.to_string(),
            _ => false,
        }
    }
}

impl Eq for HandleResult {}

/// Supervision strategy for handling child actor errors.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SupervisionStrategy {
    /// Resume the failed actor without any action.
    Resume,
    /// Restart the failed actor.
    Restart,
    /// Stop the failed actor.
    Stop,
    /// Escalate the error to the parent supervisor.
    Escalate,
}

impl Default for SupervisionStrategy {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::Resume
    }
}

/// The core trait that all actors must implement.
///
/// An actor is a self-contained unit that:
/// - Has a unique identity (ActorId)
/// - Receives and handles messages
/// - Can send messages to other actors
/// - Optionally renders visual content
/// - Can have parent/child relationships with other actors
///
/// # Thread Safety
///
/// Actors must be `Send + Sync` because:
/// - The actor registry may be shared across threads
/// - Message passing can occur from any thread via InboxHandle
/// - The render thread may call `render()` while the main thread processes messages
pub trait Actor: Send + Sync {
    /// Returns this actor's unique identifier.
    fn id(&self) -> ActorId;

    /// Sets this actor's identifier. Called by the registry during spawn.
    fn set_id(&mut self, id: ActorId);

    /// Returns the message types this actor can handle.
    /// Used by MessageExchange for routing broadcasts.
    fn handles(&self) -> &[TypeId];

    /// Handle an incoming message.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `msg` - The message to handle
    /// * `ctx` - Context providing access to system services
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// Result indicating whether the message was handled.
    fn handle(&mut self, msg: Message, ctx: &mut ActorContext) -> HandleResult;

    /// Render this actor's visual representation.
    ///
    /// Returns `None` if this actor has no visual component.
    fn render(&self, ctx: &RenderContext) -> Option<RenderNode> {
        let _ = ctx;
        None
    }

    /// Returns the IDs of this actor's children.
    fn children(&self) -> &[ActorId] {
        &[]
    }

    /// Returns the ID of this actor's parent, if any.
    fn parent(&self) -> Option<ActorId> {
        None
    }

    /// Sets the parent of this actor.
    fn set_parent(&mut self, _parent: Option<ActorId>) {}

    /// Called when this actor is spawned into the system.
    fn on_spawn(&mut self, _ctx: &mut ActorContext) {}

    /// Called when this actor is about to be despawned.
    fn on_despawn(&mut self, _ctx: &mut ActorContext) {}

    /// Called when a child actor reports an error.
    ///
    /// The default implementation returns `Escalate` to propagate
    /// errors up the supervision hierarchy.
    fn on_child_error(
        &mut self,
        _child: ActorId,
        _error: &ActorError,
        _ctx: &mut ActorContext,
    ) -> SupervisionStrategy {
        SupervisionStrategy::Escalate
    }

    /// Returns the name of this actor type (for debugging).
    fn type_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        std::any::type_name::<Self>()
    }
}

/// Context for rendering operations.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct RenderContext {
    /// Current time for animations (in seconds).
    pub time: f64,
    /// Scale factor for high-DPI displays.
    pub scale_factor: f64,
    /// Available width for rendering.
    pub width: f32,
    /// Available height for rendering.
    pub height: f32,
}

impl RenderContext {
    /// Create a new render context.
    ///
    /// Invalid scale_factor (<=0, NaN, Inf) defaults to 1.0.
    /// Width and height are clamped to non-negative values.
    pub fn new(time: f64, scale_factor: f64, width: f32, height: f32) -> Self {
        Self {
            time,
            scale_factor: if scale_factor.is_finite() && scale_factor > 0.0 {
                scale_factor
            } else {
                1.0
            },
            width: width.max(0.0),
            height: height.max(0.0),
        }
    }
}

impl Default for RenderContext {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            time: 0.0,
            scale_factor: 1.0,
            width: 800.0,
            height: 600.0,
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn handle_result_equality() {
        assert_eq!(HandleResult::Handled, HandleResult::Handled);
        assert_eq!(HandleResult::NotHandled, HandleResult::NotHandled);
        assert_eq!(
            HandleResult::error("test"),
            HandleResult::error("test")
        );
        assert_ne!(HandleResult::Handled, HandleResult::NotHandled);
    }

    #[test]
    fn actor_error_display() {
        let err = ActorError::Internal("test error".into());
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "internal error: test error");

        let err = ActorError::UnsupportedMessage("FooMsg".into());
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "unsupported message type: FooMsg");
    }

    #[test]
    fn handle_result_helpers() {
        assert!(HandleResult::error("test").is_error());
        assert!(!HandleResult::Handled.is_error());
        assert!(!HandleResult::NotHandled.is_error());

        assert!(HandleResult::Handled.was_handled());
        assert!(HandleResult::error("test").was_handled());
        assert!(!HandleResult::NotHandled.was_handled());
    }
}

# src/actor/context.rs

```rust
use std::any::TypeId;

use super::actor::ActorId;
use super::mailbox::InboxHandle;
use super::message::{Message, MessagePayload};

/// Context provided to actors during message handling.
///
/// This is the actor's view of the system - it provides access to:
/// - Sending messages to other actors
/// - Spawning/despawning actors
/// - Querying the actor hierarchy
///
/// Note: Context queues have maximum capacities to prevent unbounded memory growth.
/// If a capacity is exceeded, the operation returns false or is ignored.
pub struct ActorContext {
    /// The ID of the actor being processed.
    pub current_actor: ActorId,
    /// Outgoing messages to be routed after handling.
    outgoing: Vec<Message>,
    /// Actors to be spawned after handling.
    spawn_requests: Vec<SpawnRequest>,
    /// Actors to be despawned after handling.
    despawn_requests: Vec<ActorId>,
    /// Inbox handles for direct message delivery.
    inbox_handles: Vec<(ActorId, InboxHandle)>,
    /// Handler registrations (actor_id, message_type).
    handlers: Vec<(ActorId, TypeId)>,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for ActorContext {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("ActorContext")
            .field("current_actor", &self.current_actor)
            .field("outgoing_count", &self.outgoing.len())
            .field("spawn_requests_count", &self.spawn_requests.len())
            .field("despawn_requests_count", &self.despawn_requests.len())
            .field("inbox_handles_count", &self.inbox_handles.len())
            .field("handlers_count", &self.handlers.len())
            .finish()
    }
}

impl ActorContext {
    /// Maximum outgoing messages per context.
    pub const MAX_OUTGOING: usize = 1024;
    /// Maximum spawn requests per context.
    pub const MAX_SPAWN_REQUESTS: usize = 256;
    /// Maximum despawn requests per context.
    pub const MAX_DESPAWN_REQUESTS: usize = 256;
    /// Maximum inbox handle registrations per context.
    pub const MAX_INBOX_HANDLES: usize = 256;
    /// Maximum handler registrations per context.
    pub const MAX_HANDLER_REGISTRATIONS: usize = 256;
}

/// Request to spawn a new actor.
pub struct SpawnRequest {
    pub actor: Box<dyn FnOnce() -> Box<dyn super::Actor>>,
    pub parent: Option<ActorId>,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for SpawnRequest {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("SpawnRequest")
            .field("parent", &self.parent)
            .field("actor", &"<factory closure>")
            .finish()
    }
}

impl ActorContext {
    /// Create a new context for the given actor.
    pub fn new(current_actor: ActorId) -> Self {
        Self {
            current_actor,
            outgoing: Vec::new(),
            spawn_requests: Vec::new(),
            despawn_requests: Vec::new(),
            inbox_handles: Vec::new(),
            handlers: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Send a message to a specific actor.
    ///
    /// Returns `true` if the message was queued, `false` if the outgoing queue is full.
    pub fn send<T: MessagePayload>(&mut self, target: ActorId, payload: T) -> bool {
        if self.outgoing.len() >= Self::MAX_OUTGOING {
            log::warn!(
                "Outgoing message queue full for actor {:?}, dropping message",
                self.current_actor
            );
            return false;
        }
        let msg = Message::new(target, payload, self.current_actor);
        self.outgoing.push(msg);
        true
    }

    /// Broadcast a message (routed via MessageExchange).
    ///
    /// Returns `true` if the message was queued, `false` if the outgoing queue is full.
    pub fn broadcast<T: MessagePayload>(&mut self, payload: T) -> bool {
        if self.outgoing.len() >= Self::MAX_OUTGOING {
            log::warn!(
                "Outgoing message queue full for actor {:?}, dropping broadcast",
                self.current_actor
            );
            return false;
        }
        let msg = Message::broadcast(payload, self.current_actor);
        self.outgoing.push(msg);
        true
    }

    /// Queue a raw message for sending.
    ///
    /// Returns `true` if the message was queued, `false` if the outgoing queue is full.
    pub fn send_raw(&mut self, msg: Message) -> bool {
        if self.outgoing.len() >= Self::MAX_OUTGOING {
            log::warn!(
                "Outgoing message queue full for actor {:?}, dropping raw message",
                self.current_actor
            );
            return false;
        }
        self.outgoing.push(msg);
        true
    }

    /// Request to spawn a new actor.
    ///
    /// The actor will be spawned after the current message handling completes.
    /// Returns `true` if the request was queued, `false` if the spawn queue is full.
    pub fn spawn<F, A>(&mut self, factory: F) -> bool
    where
        F: FnOnce() -> A + 'static,
        A: super::Actor + 'static,
    {
        if self.spawn_requests.len() >= Self::MAX_SPAWN_REQUESTS {
            log::warn!(
                "Spawn request queue full for actor {:?}, ignoring spawn",
                self.current_actor
            );
            return false;
        }
        self.spawn_requests.push(SpawnRequest {
            actor: Box::new(move || Box::new(factory())),
            parent: None,
        });
        true
    }

    /// Request to spawn a new actor as a child of the current actor.
    ///
    /// Returns `true` if the request was queued, `false` if the spawn queue is full.
    pub fn spawn_child<F, A>(&mut self, factory: F) -> bool
    where
        F: FnOnce() -> A + 'static,
        A: super::Actor + 'static,
    {
        if self.spawn_requests.len() >= Self::MAX_SPAWN_REQUESTS {
            log::warn!(
                "Spawn request queue full for actor {:?}, ignoring spawn_child",
                self.current_actor
            );
            return false;
        }
        self.spawn_requests.push(SpawnRequest {
            actor: Box::new(move || Box::new(factory())),
            parent: Some(self.current_actor),
        });
        true
    }

    /// Request to despawn an actor.
    ///
    /// Returns `true` if the request was queued, `false` if the despawn queue is full.
    pub fn despawn(&mut self, id: ActorId) -> bool {
        if self.despawn_requests.len() >= Self::MAX_DESPAWN_REQUESTS {
            log::warn!(
                "Despawn request queue full for actor {:?}, ignoring despawn of {:?}",
                self.current_actor,
                id
            );
            return false;
        }
        self.despawn_requests.push(id);
        true
    }

    /// Request to despawn the current actor (self-destruct).
    ///
    /// Returns `true` if the request was queued, `false` if the despawn queue is full.
    pub fn despawn_self(&mut self) -> bool {
        if self.despawn_requests.len() >= Self::MAX_DESPAWN_REQUESTS {
            log::warn!(
                "Despawn request queue full for actor {:?}, ignoring despawn_self",
                self.current_actor
            );
            return false;
        }
        self.despawn_requests.push(self.current_actor);
        true
    }

    /// Register an inbox handle for direct message delivery.
    ///
    /// Returns `true` if registered, `false` if the inbox handle queue is full.
    pub fn register_inbox(&mut self, id: ActorId, handle: InboxHandle) -> bool {
        if self.inbox_handles.len() >= Self::MAX_INBOX_HANDLES {
            log::warn!(
                "Inbox handle registration queue full for actor {:?}",
                self.current_actor
            );
            return false;
        }
        self.inbox_handles.push((id, handle));
        true
    }

    /// Register a message type handler for an actor.
    ///
    /// Returns `true` if registered, `false` if the handler registration queue is full.
    pub fn register_handler(&mut self, id: ActorId, msg_type: TypeId) -> bool {
        if self.handlers.len() >= Self::MAX_HANDLER_REGISTRATIONS {
            log::warn!(
                "Handler registration queue full for actor {:?}",
                self.current_actor
            );
            return false;
        }
        self.handlers.push((id, msg_type));
        true
    }

    /// Take all outgoing messages.
    pub fn take_outgoing(&mut self) -> Vec<Message> {
        std::mem::take(&mut self.outgoing)
    }

    /// Take all spawn requests.
    pub fn take_spawn_requests(&mut self) -> Vec<SpawnRequest> {
        std::mem::take(&mut self.spawn_requests)
    }

    /// Take all despawn requests.
    pub fn take_despawn_requests(&mut self) -> Vec<ActorId> {
        std::mem::take(&mut self.despawn_requests)
    }

    /// Take all inbox handle registrations.
    pub fn take_inbox_handles(&mut self) -> Vec<(ActorId, InboxHandle)> {
        std::mem::take(&mut self.inbox_handles)
    }

    /// Take all handler registrations.
    pub fn take_handlers(&mut self) -> Vec<(ActorId, TypeId)> {
        std::mem::take(&mut self.handlers)
    }

    /// Check if there are any pending operations.
    pub fn has_pending(&self) -> bool {
        !self.outgoing.is_empty()
            || !self.spawn_requests.is_empty()
            || !self.despawn_requests.is_empty()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use slotmap::SlotMap;

    #[test]
    fn context_send_message() {
        let mut actors: SlotMap<ActorId, ()> = SlotMap::with_key();
        let current = actors.insert(());
        let target = actors.insert(());

        let mut ctx = ActorContext::new(current);
        ctx.send(target, 42i32);

        let outgoing = ctx.take_outgoing();
        assert_eq!(outgoing.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(outgoing[0].target, Some(target));
        assert_eq!(outgoing[0].source, current);
    }

    #[test]
    fn context_broadcast() {
        let mut actors: SlotMap<ActorId, ()> = SlotMap::with_key();
        let current = actors.insert(());

        let mut ctx = ActorContext::new(current);
        ctx.broadcast("hello");

        let outgoing = ctx.take_outgoing();
        assert_eq!(outgoing.len(), 1);
        assert!(outgoing[0].target.is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn context_despawn_self() {
        let mut actors: SlotMap<ActorId, ()> = SlotMap::with_key();
        let current = actors.insert(());

        let mut ctx = ActorContext::new(current);
        ctx.despawn_self();

        let despawns = ctx.take_despawn_requests();
        assert_eq!(despawns.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(despawns[0], current);
    }
}

# src/actor/exchange.rs

```rust
use std::any::TypeId;
use std::collections::HashMap;

use smallvec::SmallVec;

use super::actor::{Actor, ActorId, HandleResult, RenderContext};
use super::context::ActorContext;
use super::message::Message;
use crate::graphics::RenderNode;

/// MessageExchange is a special actor that routes broadcast messages.
///
/// When an actor sends a message with `target: None`, the system finds
/// the nearest MessageExchange in the actor hierarchy and uses it to
/// broadcast the message to all actors that handle that message type.
///
/// This provides a pub/sub pattern where actors can communicate without
/// needing to know each other's IDs. It's similar to event bubbling in
/// traditional UI frameworks, but completely generic.
///
/// # Example Hierarchy
///
/// ```text
/// Root (MessageExchange)
///   ├── Panel A
///   │   ├── Button (broadcasts "Click")
///   │   └── Label (handles "Click")
///   └── Panel B (MessageExchange)
///       ├── Button (broadcasts "Click")
///       └── Label (handles "Click")
/// ```
///
/// In this example:
/// - Panel A's Button broadcasts to Root's MessageExchange
/// - Panel B's Button broadcasts to Panel B's MessageExchange (nearest)
/// - Messages stay scoped to their nearest exchange
pub struct MessageExchange {
    id: ActorId,
    parent: Option<ActorId>,
    children: SmallVec<[ActorId; 8]>,
    /// Mapping from message type to actors that handle it.
    handlers: HashMap<TypeId, SmallVec<[ActorId; 8]>>,
    /// Whether to propagate unhandled messages to parent exchange.
    propagate_unhandled: bool,
}

impl MessageExchange {
    /// Create a new message exchange.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            id: ActorId::default(),
            parent: None,
            children: SmallVec::new(),
            handlers: HashMap::new(),
            propagate_unhandled: false,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new message exchange that propagates unhandled messages.
    pub fn with_propagation() -> Self {
        Self {
            propagate_unhandled: true,
            ..Self::new()
        }
    }

    /// Maximum handlers per message type.
    pub const MAX_HANDLERS_PER_TYPE: usize = 256;

    /// Register a handler for a message type.
    ///
    /// Returns `true` if the handler was registered, `false` if:
    /// - The handler is already registered for this type
    /// - The maximum handlers per type limit has been reached
    pub fn register_handler(&mut self, msg_type: TypeId, actor: ActorId) -> bool {
        let handlers = self.handlers.entry(msg_type).or_default();
        if handlers.contains(&actor) {
            return false; // Already registered
        }
        if handlers.len() >= Self::MAX_HANDLERS_PER_TYPE {
            log::warn!(
                "MessageExchange {:?}: max handlers reached for message type",
                self.id
            );
            return false;
        }
        handlers.push(actor);
        true
    }

    /// Unregister a handler for a message type.
    pub fn unregister_handler(&mut self, msg_type: TypeId, actor: ActorId) {
        if let Some(handlers) = self.handlers.get_mut(&msg_type) {
            handlers.retain(|id| *id != actor);
        }
    }

    /// Unregister all handlers for an actor.
    pub fn unregister_actor(&mut self, actor: ActorId) {
        for handlers in self.handlers.values_mut() {
            handlers.retain(|id| *id != actor);
        }
    }

    /// Get handlers for a message type.
    pub fn handlers_for(&self, msg_type: TypeId) -> &[ActorId] {
        self.handlers
            .get(&msg_type)
            .map(|v| v.as_slice())
            .unwrap_or(&[])
    }

    /// Maximum children per MessageExchange.
    pub const MAX_CHILDREN: usize = 1024;

    /// Add a child actor.
    ///
    /// Returns `true` if the child was added, `false` if:
    /// - The child is already present
    /// - The maximum children limit has been reached
    pub fn add_child(&mut self, child: ActorId) -> bool {
        if self.children.contains(&child) {
            return false; // Already a child
        }
        if self.children.len() >= Self::MAX_CHILDREN {
            log::warn!(
                "MessageExchange {:?}: max children capacity reached",
                self.id
            );
            return false;
        }
        self.children.push(child);
        true
    }

    /// Remove a child actor.
    pub fn remove_child(&mut self, child: ActorId) {
        self.children.retain(|id| *id != child);
    }
}

impl Default for MessageExchange {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl Actor for MessageExchange {
    fn id(&self) -> ActorId {
        self.id
    }

    fn set_id(&mut self, id: ActorId) {
        self.id = id;
    }

    fn handles(&self) -> &[TypeId] {
        // MessageExchange handles all message types (it's a router)
        // but we return empty because we don't want to be registered
        // as a handler for specific types - we're a meta-handler.
        &[]
    }

    fn handle(&mut self, msg: Message, ctx: &mut ActorContext) -> HandleResult {
        // Route broadcast messages to registered handlers
        // Note: handlers_for returns a reference, so we need to collect to avoid borrow issues
        let handlers: SmallVec<[ActorId; 8]> = self
            .handlers
            .get(&msg.payload_type)
            .cloned()
            .unwrap_or_default();

        if handlers.is_empty() {
            if self.propagate_unhandled {
                // Propagate to parent exchange
                if let Some(parent) = self.parent {
                    ctx.send_raw(msg.retarget(parent));
                    return HandleResult::Handled;
                }
            }
            return HandleResult::NotHandled;
        }

        // Route to ALL handlers using Arc-based message sharing
        // Message is cloned using Arc internally, so this is efficient
        for &handler_id in &handlers {
            if handler_id != msg.source {
                // Clone the message (Arc-based, efficient sharing)
                let cloned = msg.clone().retarget(handler_id);
                ctx.send_raw(cloned);
            }
        }

        HandleResult::Handled
    }

    fn render(&self, _ctx: &RenderContext) -> Option<RenderNode> {
        None
    }

    fn children(&self) -> &[ActorId] {
        &self.children
    }

    fn parent(&self) -> Option<ActorId> {
        self.parent
    }

    fn set_parent(&mut self, parent: Option<ActorId>) {
        self.parent = parent;
    }

    fn type_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        "MessageExchange"
    }
}

/// Message to register a handler with an exchange.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct RegisterHandler {
    pub msg_type: TypeId,
    pub actor: ActorId,
}

/// Message to unregister a handler from an exchange.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct UnregisterHandler {
    pub msg_type: TypeId,
    pub actor: ActorId,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn register_and_lookup_handler() {
        let mut exchange = MessageExchange::new();
        let msg_type = TypeId::of::<i32>();

        // Create a fake actor id using slotmap
        use slotmap::SlotMap;
        let mut actors: SlotMap<ActorId, ()> = SlotMap::with_key();
        let handler_id = actors.insert(());

        exchange.register_handler(msg_type, handler_id);
        assert_eq!(exchange.handlers_for(msg_type), &[handler_id]);

        exchange.unregister_handler(msg_type, handler_id);
        assert!(exchange.handlers_for(msg_type).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn unregister_actor_removes_all_handlers() {
        let mut exchange = MessageExchange::new();

        use slotmap::SlotMap;
        let mut actors: SlotMap<ActorId, ()> = SlotMap::with_key();
        let handler_id = actors.insert(());

        exchange.register_handler(TypeId::of::<i32>(), handler_id);
        exchange.register_handler(TypeId::of::<String>(), handler_id);

        exchange.unregister_actor(handler_id);

        assert!(exchange.handlers_for(TypeId::of::<i32>()).is_empty());
        assert!(exchange.handlers_for(TypeId::of::<String>()).is_empty());
    }
}

# src/actor/mailbox.rs

```rust
use crossbeam::queue::ArrayQueue;
use std::sync::Arc;

use super::message::Message;

/// Default capacity for mailboxes.
pub const DEFAULT_MAILBOX_CAPACITY: usize = 256;

/// A lock-free mailbox for actor message passing.
///
/// Uses a bounded lock-free queue (ArrayQueue) for both inbox and outbox.
/// This ensures that message passing never blocks or requires locks,
/// which is critical for real-time audio applications.
pub struct Mailbox {
    /// Incoming messages for this actor.
    inbox: Arc<ArrayQueue<Message>>,
    /// Outgoing messages from this actor.
    outbox: Arc<ArrayQueue<Message>>,
    /// Capacity of the queues.
    capacity: usize,
}

impl Mailbox {
    /// Create a new mailbox with the default capacity.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::with_capacity(DEFAULT_MAILBOX_CAPACITY)
    }

    /// Create a new mailbox with a specific capacity.
    ///
    /// Capacity is clamped to a minimum of 1 to ensure the mailbox can receive messages.
    pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> Self {
        let capacity = capacity.max(1); // Ensure at least capacity of 1
        Self {
            inbox: Arc::new(ArrayQueue::new(capacity)),
            outbox: Arc::new(ArrayQueue::new(capacity)),
            capacity,
        }
    }

    /// Try to push a message to the inbox.
    ///
    /// Returns `Err(msg)` if the inbox is full.
    pub fn push_inbox(&self, msg: Message) -> Result<(), Message> {
        self.inbox.push(msg)
    }

    /// Try to pop a message from the inbox.
    pub fn pop_inbox(&self) -> Option<Message> {
        self.inbox.pop()
    }

    /// Try to push a message to the outbox.
    ///
    /// Returns `Err(msg)` if the outbox is full.
    pub fn push_outbox(&self, msg: Message) -> Result<(), Message> {
        self.outbox.push(msg)
    }

    /// Try to pop a message from the outbox.
    pub fn pop_outbox(&self) -> Option<Message> {
        self.outbox.pop()
    }

    /// Check if the inbox is empty.
    pub fn inbox_is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.inbox.is_empty()
    }

    /// Check if the outbox is empty.
    pub fn outbox_is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.outbox.is_empty()
    }

    /// Get the number of messages in the inbox.
    pub fn inbox_len(&self) -> usize {
        self.inbox.len()
    }

    /// Get the number of messages in the outbox.
    pub fn outbox_len(&self) -> usize {
        self.outbox.len()
    }

    /// Get the capacity of the mailbox.
    pub fn capacity(&self) -> usize {
        self.capacity
    }

    /// Get a handle to the inbox for external producers.
    pub fn inbox_handle(&self) -> InboxHandle {
        InboxHandle {
            queue: Arc::clone(&self.inbox),
        }
    }

    /// Get a handle to the outbox for external consumers.
    pub fn outbox_handle(&self) -> OutboxHandle {
        OutboxHandle {
            queue: Arc::clone(&self.outbox),
        }
    }

    /// Drain all messages from the inbox into a vector.
    pub fn drain_inbox(&self) -> Vec<Message> {
        let mut messages = Vec::with_capacity(self.inbox.len());
        while let Some(msg) = self.inbox.pop() {
            messages.push(msg);
        }
        messages
    }

    /// Drain all messages from the outbox into a vector.
    pub fn drain_outbox(&self) -> Vec<Message> {
        let mut messages = Vec::with_capacity(self.outbox.len());
        while let Some(msg) = self.outbox.pop() {
            messages.push(msg);
        }
        messages
    }
}

impl Default for Mailbox {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// Handle for pushing messages to an actor's inbox.
///
/// This can be shared across threads to allow external producers
/// to send messages to an actor.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct InboxHandle {
    queue: Arc<ArrayQueue<Message>>,
}

impl InboxHandle {
    /// Try to push a message to the inbox.
    pub fn push(&self, msg: Message) -> Result<(), Message> {
        self.queue.push(msg)
    }

    /// Check if the inbox is full.
    pub fn is_full(&self) -> bool {
        self.queue.is_full()
    }

    /// Get the current length of the inbox.
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.queue.len()
    }

    /// Check if the inbox is empty.
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.queue.is_empty()
    }
}

/// Handle for consuming messages from an actor's outbox.
///
/// This can be shared across threads to allow external consumers
/// to receive messages from an actor.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct OutboxHandle {
    queue: Arc<ArrayQueue<Message>>,
}

impl OutboxHandle {
    /// Try to pop a message from the outbox.
    pub fn pop(&self) -> Option<Message> {
        self.queue.pop()
    }

    /// Check if the outbox is empty.
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.queue.is_empty()
    }

    /// Get the current length of the outbox.
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.queue.len()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use slotmap::SlotMap;
    use std::sync::Arc;
    use std::thread;

    use crate::actor::ActorId;

    struct DummyPayload(i32);

    fn make_test_message(value: i32) -> Message {
        let mut actors: SlotMap<ActorId, ()> = SlotMap::with_key();
        let source = actors.insert(());
        let target = actors.insert(());
        Message::new(target, DummyPayload(value), source)
    }

    #[test]
    fn mailbox_basic_operations() {
        let mailbox = Mailbox::new();

        assert!(mailbox.inbox_is_empty());
        assert!(mailbox.outbox_is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn mailbox_push_pop() {
        let mailbox = Mailbox::new();
        let msg = make_test_message(42);

        assert!(mailbox.push_inbox(msg).is_ok());
        assert!(!mailbox.inbox_is_empty());
        assert_eq!(mailbox.inbox_len(), 1);

        let popped = mailbox.pop_inbox();
        assert!(popped.is_some());
        assert!(mailbox.inbox_is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn mailbox_capacity() {
        let mailbox = Mailbox::with_capacity(2);
        assert_eq!(mailbox.capacity(), 2);

        // Fill the mailbox
        assert!(mailbox.push_inbox(make_test_message(1)).is_ok());
        assert!(mailbox.push_inbox(make_test_message(2)).is_ok());

        // Third push should fail (backpressure)
        let result = mailbox.push_inbox(make_test_message(3));
        assert!(result.is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn inbox_handle_sharing() {
        let mailbox = Mailbox::new();
        let handle1 = mailbox.inbox_handle();
        let handle2 = mailbox.inbox_handle();

        // Both handles should work
        assert!(handle1.is_empty());
        assert!(handle2.is_empty());

        // Push via handle1
        handle1.push(make_test_message(1)).unwrap();

        // Both handles see the message
        assert!(!handle1.is_empty());
        assert!(!handle2.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(handle1.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(handle2.len(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn concurrent_push_single_mailbox() {
        let mailbox = Arc::new(Mailbox::with_capacity(1000));
        let handle = mailbox.inbox_handle();

        let mut handles = Vec::new();
        const NUM_THREADS: usize = 4;
        const MESSAGES_PER_THREAD: usize = 100;

        for _ in 0..NUM_THREADS {
            let h = handle.clone();
            handles.push(thread::spawn(move || {
                let mut success_count = 0;
                for i in 0..MESSAGES_PER_THREAD {
                    let msg = make_test_message(i as i32);
                    if h.push(msg).is_ok() {
                        success_count += 1;
                    }
                }
                success_count
            }));
        }

        let total_pushed: usize = handles.into_iter().map(|h| h.join().unwrap()).sum();

        // All messages should have been pushed (mailbox has capacity 1000)
        assert_eq!(total_pushed, NUM_THREADS * MESSAGES_PER_THREAD);
        assert_eq!(mailbox.inbox_len(), NUM_THREADS * MESSAGES_PER_THREAD);
    }

    #[test]
    fn concurrent_push_pop() {
        use std::time::Duration;

        let mailbox = Arc::new(Mailbox::with_capacity(100));
        let handle = mailbox.inbox_handle();

        const NUM_MESSAGES: usize = 1000;

        // Producer thread
        let producer_handle = handle.clone();
        let producer = thread::spawn(move || {
            let mut success = 0;
            let mut backoff = 1;
            for i in 0..NUM_MESSAGES {
                let msg = make_test_message(i as i32);
                // Retry with exponential backoff if full
                loop {
                    match producer_handle.push(msg.clone()) {
                        Ok(()) => {
                            success += 1;
                            backoff = 1; // Reset backoff on success
                            break;
                        }
                        Err(_) => {
                            // Exponential backoff with cap
                            thread::sleep(Duration::from_micros(backoff));
                            backoff = (backoff * 2).min(1000);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            success
        });

        // Consumer thread
        let consumer_mailbox = Arc::clone(&mailbox);
        let consumer = thread::spawn(move || {
            let mut consumed = 0;
            let mut backoff = 1;
            while consumed < NUM_MESSAGES {
                if consumer_mailbox.pop_inbox().is_some() {
                    consumed += 1;
                    backoff = 1; // Reset backoff on success
                } else {
                    // Exponential backoff with cap
                    thread::sleep(Duration::from_micros(backoff));
                    backoff = (backoff * 2).min(1000);
                }
            }
            consumed
        });

        let produced = producer.join().unwrap();
        let consumed = consumer.join().unwrap();

        assert_eq!(produced, NUM_MESSAGES);
        assert_eq!(consumed, NUM_MESSAGES);
        assert!(mailbox.inbox_is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn drain_returns_all_messages() {
        let mailbox = Mailbox::new();

        for i in 0..10 {
            mailbox.push_inbox(make_test_message(i)).unwrap();
        }

        let drained = mailbox.drain_inbox();
        assert_eq!(drained.len(), 10);
        assert!(mailbox.inbox_is_empty());
    }
}

use std::any::{Any, TypeId};
use std::fmt;
use std::sync::Arc;

use super::actor::ActorId;

/// Marker trait for message payloads.
pub trait MessagePayload: Any + Send + Sync {}

/// Blanket implementation for all types that satisfy the bounds.
impl<T: Any + Send + Sync> MessagePayload for T {}

/// Shared payload wrapper for broadcast messages.
///
/// Uses Arc internally to allow efficient sharing across multiple recipients.
/// When a message is cloned (e.g., for broadcasting), the payload is shared
/// via Arc rather than deeply copied, making broadcast operations efficient.
///
/// # Thread Safety
///
/// This type is always constructed via `SharedPayload::new<T>()` which
/// requires `T: Any + Send + Sync`, ensuring thread-safety of the inner value.
/// The Arc provides atomic reference counting for safe concurrent access.
///
/// # Performance
///
/// Cloning a SharedPayload is O(1) - it only increments the Arc reference count.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct SharedPayload {
    inner: Arc<dyn Any + Send + Sync>,
    type_id: TypeId,
    type_name: &'static str,
}

impl SharedPayload {
    /// Create a new shared payload.
    pub fn new<T: MessagePayload>(payload: T) -> Self {
        Self {
            inner: Arc::new(payload),
            type_id: TypeId::of::<T>(),
            type_name: std::any::type_name::<T>(),
        }
    }

    /// Try to downcast to a specific type.
    pub fn downcast_ref<T: 'static>(&self) -> Option<&T> {
        self.inner.downcast_ref::<T>()
    }

    /// Check if the payload is of a specific type.
    pub fn is<T: 'static>(&self) -> bool {
        self.type_id == TypeId::of::<T>()
    }

    /// Get the type ID.
    pub fn type_id(&self) -> TypeId {
        self.type_id
    }

    /// Get the type name for debugging.
    pub fn type_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        self.type_name
    }
}

impl fmt::Debug for SharedPayload {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "SharedPayload({})", self.type_name)
    }
}

/// A message sent between actors.
///
/// Messages can be either targeted (sent to a specific actor) or broadcast
/// (sent to all actors that handle the message type).
///
/// For broadcast messages, the payload uses Arc-based sharing to efficiently
/// deliver the same message to multiple recipients without cloning the data.
pub struct Message {
    /// Target actor. If `None`, the message is a broadcast
    /// that will be routed through a MessageExchange.
    pub target: Option<ActorId>,

    /// The type ID of the payload, used for routing.
    pub payload_type: TypeId,

    /// The actual message content stored as Arc for sharing.
    payload: SharedPayload,

    /// The actor that sent this message.
    pub source: ActorId,
}

impl Clone for Message {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Self {
            target: self.target,
            payload_type: self.payload_type,
            payload: self.payload.clone(),
            source: self.source,
        }
    }
}

impl Message {
    /// Create a new targeted message.
    pub fn new<T: MessagePayload>(target: ActorId, payload: T, source: ActorId) -> Self {
        let shared = SharedPayload::new(payload);
        Self {
            target: Some(target),
            payload_type: shared.type_id(),
            payload: shared,
            source,
        }
    }

    /// Create a new broadcast message (no specific target).
    pub fn broadcast<T: MessagePayload>(payload: T, source: ActorId) -> Self {
        let shared = SharedPayload::new(payload);
        Self {
            target: None,
            payload_type: shared.type_id(),
            payload: shared,
            source,
        }
    }

    /// Try to downcast the payload to a specific type.
    pub fn downcast_ref<T: 'static>(&self) -> Option<&T> {
        self.payload.downcast_ref::<T>()
    }

    /// Check if the payload is of a specific type.
    pub fn is<T: 'static>(&self) -> bool {
        self.payload_type == TypeId::of::<T>()
    }

    /// Get the type name of the payload (for debugging).
    pub fn payload_type_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        self.payload.type_name()
    }

    /// Retarget this message to a specific actor.
    /// Consumes the message and returns a new one with the new target.
    pub fn retarget(self, target: ActorId) -> Self {
        Self {
            target: Some(target),
            payload_type: self.payload_type,
            payload: self.payload,
            source: self.source,
        }
    }

    /// Convert to a broadcast message (no specific target).
    pub fn into_broadcast(self) -> Self {
        Self {
            target: None,
            payload_type: self.payload_type,
            payload: self.payload,
            source: self.source,
        }
    }
}

impl fmt::Debug for Message {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("Message")
            .field("target", &self.target)
            .field("payload_type", &self.payload.type_name())
            .field("source", &self.source)
            .finish()
    }
}

// Common message types

/// Request to close/despawn an actor.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct CloseRequest;

/// Notification that an actor was spawned.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ActorSpawned {
    pub id: ActorId,
}

/// Notification that an actor was despawned.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ActorDespawned {
    pub id: ActorId,
}

/// Request a redraw of the UI.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct RedrawRequest;

/// Focus request - actor wants input focus.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct FocusRequest {
    pub actor: ActorId,
}

/// Focus changed notification.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct FocusChanged {
    pub previous: Option<ActorId>,
    pub current: Option<ActorId>,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use slotmap::SlotMap;

    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
    struct TestPayload {
        value: i32,
    }

    #[test]
    fn message_creation() {
        let mut actors: SlotMap<ActorId, ()> = SlotMap::with_key();
        let source = actors.insert(());
        let target = actors.insert(());

        let msg = Message::new(target, TestPayload { value: 42 }, source);

        assert_eq!(msg.target, Some(target));
        assert_eq!(msg.source, source);
        assert!(msg.is::<TestPayload>());
    }

    #[test]
    fn message_downcast() {
        let mut actors: SlotMap<ActorId, ()> = SlotMap::with_key();
        let source = actors.insert(());
        let target = actors.insert(());

        let msg = Message::new(target, TestPayload { value: 42 }, source);

        let payload = msg.downcast_ref::<TestPayload>().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(payload.value, 42);
    }

    #[test]
    fn broadcast_message() {
        let mut actors: SlotMap<ActorId, ()> = SlotMap::with_key();
        let source = actors.insert(());

        let msg = Message::broadcast(TestPayload { value: 100 }, source);

        assert!(msg.target.is_none());
        assert!(msg.is::<TestPayload>());
    }

    #[test]
    fn message_clone_shares_payload() {
        let mut actors: SlotMap<ActorId, ()> = SlotMap::with_key();
        let source = actors.insert(());

        let msg1 = Message::broadcast(TestPayload { value: 42 }, source);
        let msg2 = msg1.clone();

        // Both should have the same payload
        let p1 = msg1.downcast_ref::<TestPayload>().unwrap();
        let p2 = msg2.downcast_ref::<TestPayload>().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(p1.value, p2.value);
    }
}

```rust
use std::any::TypeId;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};

use parking_lot::RwLock;
use slotmap::SlotMap;
use smallvec::SmallVec;

use super::actor::{Actor, ActorError, ActorId, HandleResult, SupervisionStrategy};
use super::context::ActorContext;
use super::mailbox::{InboxHandle, Mailbox};
use super::message::Message;

/// Metrics for tracking actor system health.
///
/// Note: Counters use wrapping addition and will wrap around at `u64::MAX`.
/// For long-running applications, consider periodic snapshotting if overflow
/// could be an issue (though 2^64 operations would take millennia at typical rates).
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct RegistryMetrics {
    /// Total messages delivered successfully (wraps at u64::MAX).
    pub messages_delivered: AtomicU64,
    /// Total messages dropped due to full mailboxes (wraps at u64::MAX).
    pub messages_dropped: AtomicU64,
    /// Total broadcast messages sent (wraps at u64::MAX).
    pub broadcasts_sent: AtomicU64,
    /// Total actors spawned (wraps at u64::MAX).
    pub actors_spawned: AtomicU64,
    /// Total actors despawned (wraps at u64::MAX).
    pub actors_despawned: AtomicU64,
    /// Total errors during message handling (wraps at u64::MAX).
    pub handle_errors: AtomicU64,
}

impl RegistryMetrics {
    /// Get a snapshot of the current metrics.
    ///
    /// Uses `Ordering::Acquire` to ensure all preceding writes are visible,
    /// providing a consistent view of the metrics at the time of the snapshot.
    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> MetricsSnapshot {
        MetricsSnapshot {
            messages_delivered: self.messages_delivered.load(Ordering::Acquire),
            messages_dropped: self.messages_dropped.load(Ordering::Acquire),
            broadcasts_sent: self.broadcasts_sent.load(Ordering::Acquire),
            actors_spawned: self.actors_spawned.load(Ordering::Acquire),
            actors_despawned: self.actors_despawned.load(Ordering::Acquire),
            handle_errors: self.handle_errors.load(Ordering::Acquire),
        }
    }
}

/// A point-in-time snapshot of registry metrics.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct MetricsSnapshot {
    pub messages_delivered: u64,
    pub messages_dropped: u64,
    pub broadcasts_sent: u64,
    pub actors_spawned: u64,
    pub actors_despawned: u64,
    pub handle_errors: u64,
}

/// Result of sending a message.
#[must_use = "send result should be checked for delivery failure or backpressure"]
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum SendResult {
    /// Message was delivered successfully.
    Delivered,
    /// Mailbox is full - message returned for retry or handling.
    MailboxFull(Message),
    /// Target actor was not found - message returned.
    ActorNotFound(Message),
}

impl SendResult {
    /// Check if the send was successful.
    pub fn is_ok(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, SendResult::Delivered)
    }

    /// Check if the send failed.
    pub fn is_err(&self) -> bool {
        !self.is_ok()
    }
}

/// Entry for an actor in the registry.
struct ActorEntry {
    actor: Box<dyn Actor>,
    mailbox: Mailbox,
    parent: Option<ActorId>,
    children: SmallVec<[ActorId; 4]>,
    /// Flag indicating this actor has pending messages.
    has_pending: bool,
}

/// Central registry managing all actors in the system.
///
/// The registry is responsible for:
/// - Storing and managing actor lifecycles
/// - Routing messages between actors
/// - Maintaining parent/child relationships
/// - Processing the actor event loop
/// - Tracking metrics for system health monitoring
pub struct ActorRegistry {
    /// All registered actors.
    actors: SlotMap<ActorId, ActorEntry>,
    /// Mapping from message type to actors that handle it.
    handlers: HashMap<TypeId, SmallVec<[ActorId; 8]>>,
    /// Inbox handles for external message delivery.
    inbox_handles: HashMap<ActorId, InboxHandle>,
    /// The root actor (if any).
    root: Option<ActorId>,
    /// Set of actor IDs with pending messages (for optimized tick).
    pending_actors: SmallVec<[ActorId; 16]>,
    /// Metrics for monitoring.
    metrics: RegistryMetrics,
}

impl ActorRegistry {
    /// Maximum distinct message types the registry can track.
    pub const MAX_MESSAGE_TYPES: usize = 4096;

    /// Create a new empty registry.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            actors: SlotMap::with_key(),
            handlers: HashMap::new(),
            inbox_handles: HashMap::new(),
            root: None,
            pending_actors: SmallVec::new(),
            metrics: RegistryMetrics::default(),
        }
    }

    /// Get the registry metrics.
    pub fn metrics(&self) -> &RegistryMetrics {
        &self.metrics
    }

    /// Spawn a new actor into the registry.
    pub fn spawn(&mut self, mut actor: Box<dyn Actor>) -> ActorId {
        let mailbox = Mailbox::new();
        let inbox_handle = mailbox.inbox_handle();

        let id = self.actors.insert_with_key(|id| {
            actor.set_id(id);
            ActorEntry {
                actor,
                mailbox,
                parent: None,
                children: SmallVec::new(),
                has_pending: false,
            }
        });

        // Register handlers (check for duplicates and capacity)
        if let Some(entry) = self.actors.get(id) {
            for &type_id in entry.actor.handles() {
                // Check capacity before adding new message type
                if !self.handlers.contains_key(&type_id)
                    && self.handlers.len() >= Self::MAX_MESSAGE_TYPES
                {
                    log::warn!(
                        "Maximum message types ({}) reached, cannot register handler for new type",
                        Self::MAX_MESSAGE_TYPES
                    );
                    continue;
                }
                let handlers = self.handlers.entry(type_id).or_default();
                if !handlers.contains(&id) {
                    handlers.push(id);
                }
            }
        }

        // Store inbox handle
        self.inbox_handles.insert(id, inbox_handle);

        // Call on_spawn
        let mut ctx = ActorContext::new(id);
        if let Some(entry) = self.actors.get_mut(id) {
            entry.actor.on_spawn(&mut ctx);
        }

        // Process any spawn-time requests
        self.process_context_requests(ctx);

        // Set as root if first actor
        if self.root.is_none() {
            self.root = Some(id);
        }

        self.metrics.actors_spawned.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        id
    }

    /// Spawn an actor with a parent.
    pub fn spawn_with_parent(&mut self, actor: Box<dyn Actor>, parent: ActorId) -> ActorId {
        let id = self.spawn(actor);

        // Set parent relationship
        if let Some(entry) = self.actors.get_mut(id) {
            entry.parent = Some(parent);
            entry.actor.set_parent(Some(parent));
        }

        // Add to parent's children
        if let Some(parent_entry) = self.actors.get_mut(parent) {
            parent_entry.children.push(id);
        }

        id
    }

    /// Despawn an actor and all its children.
    ///
    /// Uses an iterative approach to avoid stack overflow with deeply nested hierarchies.
    pub fn despawn(&mut self, id: ActorId) {
        // Collect all actors to despawn (children first, then parents)
        let mut to_despawn = Vec::new();
        let mut stack = vec![id];

        // Build the full list of actors to despawn (post-order traversal)
        while let Some(current) = stack.pop() {
            to_despawn.push(current);
            if let Some(entry) = self.actors.get(current) {
                // Push children onto stack (they'll be processed first)
                for &child in &entry.children {
                    stack.push(child);
                }
            }
        }

        // Process in reverse order (children before parents)
        for actor_id in to_despawn.into_iter().rev() {
            self.despawn_single(actor_id);
        }
    }

    /// Despawn a single actor without processing children.
    fn despawn_single(&mut self, id: ActorId) {
        // Call on_despawn
        let mut ctx = ActorContext::new(id);
        if let Some(entry) = self.actors.get_mut(id) {
            entry.actor.on_despawn(&mut ctx);
        }

        // Remove from handlers
        if let Some(entry) = self.actors.get(id) {
            for &type_id in entry.actor.handles() {
                if let Some(handlers) = self.handlers.get_mut(&type_id) {
                    handlers.retain(|h| *h != id);
                }
            }
        }

        // Clean up empty handler lists to prevent memory growth
        self.handlers.retain(|_, v| !v.is_empty());

        // Remove from parent's children
        if let Some(entry) = self.actors.get(id) {
            if let Some(parent) = entry.parent {
                if let Some(parent_entry) = self.actors.get_mut(parent) {
                    parent_entry.children.retain(|c| *c != id);
                }
            }
        }

        // Remove from pending actors list
        self.pending_actors.retain(|a| *a != id);

        // Remove inbox handle
        self.inbox_handles.remove(&id);

        // Remove actor
        self.actors.remove(id);

        // Clear root if this was it
        if self.root == Some(id) {
            self.root = None;
        }

        self.metrics.actors_despawned.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }

    /// Send a message to a specific actor.
    ///
    /// Returns `SendResult::Delivered` if the message was queued successfully,
    /// `SendResult::MailboxFull` if the mailbox is full (backpressure),
    /// or `SendResult::ActorNotFound` if the target actor doesn't exist.
    pub fn send(&mut self, msg: Message) -> SendResult {
        if let Some(target) = msg.target {
            if let Some(handle) = self.inbox_handles.get(&target) {
                match handle.push(msg) {
                    Ok(()) => {
                        // Mark actor as having pending messages
                        if let Some(entry) = self.actors.get_mut(target) {
                            if !entry.has_pending {
                                entry.has_pending = true;
                                self.pending_actors.push(target);
                            }
                        }
                        self.metrics.messages_delivered.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                        return SendResult::Delivered;
                    }
                    Err(msg) => {
                        self.metrics.messages_dropped.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                        log::warn!(
                            "Message dropped: mailbox full for actor {:?}, type: {}",
                            target,
                            msg.payload_type_name()
                        );
                        return SendResult::MailboxFull(msg);
                    }
                }
            } else {
                return SendResult::ActorNotFound(msg);
            }
        }
        self.metrics.messages_dropped.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        SendResult::ActorNotFound(msg)
    }

    /// Broadcast a message to all actors that handle its type.
    ///
    /// Messages are cloned (using Arc-based sharing) for each recipient.
    /// Returns the number of actors that received the message.
    #[must_use = "broadcast returns the number of recipients, check for delivery failures"]
    pub fn broadcast(&mut self, msg: Message) -> usize {
        // First, collect handler IDs without borrowing self mutably
        let handler_ids: SmallVec<[ActorId; 8]> = self
            .handlers
            .get(&msg.payload_type)
            .map(|h| h.iter().copied().filter(|&id| id != msg.source).collect())
            .unwrap_or_default();

        if handler_ids.is_empty() {
            return 0;
        }

        let mut delivered = 0;

        // Now send to each handler
        for handler_id in handler_ids {
            // Clone the message (Arc-based, efficient)
            let cloned_msg = msg.clone().retarget(handler_id);
            if self.send(cloned_msg).is_ok() {
                delivered += 1;
            }
        }

        if delivered > 0 {
            self.metrics.broadcasts_sent.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
        delivered
    }

    /// Process one tick of the actor system.
    ///
    /// This drains all mailboxes, delivers messages, and processes
    /// any spawn/despawn requests that result from handling.
    ///
    /// Optimized to only process actors with pending messages.
    pub fn tick(&mut self) {
        // Swap out pending actors list to avoid borrow issues
        let pending = std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_actors);

        // Collect messages only from actors with pending messages
        // Use a temporary Vec to avoid borrow issues
        let mut pending_messages: Vec<(ActorId, Message)> = Vec::new();

        for &id in &pending {
            if let Some(entry) = self.actors.get_mut(id) {
                entry.has_pending = false;
                while let Some(msg) = entry.mailbox.pop_inbox() {
                    pending_messages.push((id, msg));
                }
            }
        }

        // Collect results that need post-processing
        let mut errors_to_handle: Vec<(ActorId, ActorError)> = Vec::new();
        let mut contexts_to_process: Vec<ActorContext> = Vec::new();

        // Process each message
        for (target_id, msg) in pending_messages {
            let mut ctx = ActorContext::new(target_id);

            let result = if let Some(entry) = self.actors.get_mut(target_id) {
                entry.actor.handle(msg, &mut ctx)
            } else {
                continue;
            };

            // Collect errors for later handling
            if let HandleResult::Error(ref err) = result {
                self.metrics.handle_errors.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                log::error!("Actor {:?} handle error: {}", target_id, err);
                errors_to_handle.push((target_id, err.clone()));
            }

            contexts_to_process.push(ctx);
        }

        // Process errors with supervision (after message processing loop)
        for (actor_id, error) in errors_to_handle {
            self.handle_actor_error(actor_id, error);
        }

        // Process context requests (after message processing loop)
        for ctx in contexts_to_process {
            self.process_context_requests(ctx);
        }

        // Route outgoing messages from all actors
        let mut outgoing: Vec<Message> = Vec::new();
        for (_, entry) in self.actors.iter() {
            while let Some(msg) = entry.mailbox.pop_outbox() {
                outgoing.push(msg);
            }
        }

        for msg in outgoing {
            if msg.target.is_some() {
                let _ = self.send(msg);
            } else {
                let _ = self.broadcast(msg);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Handle an actor error by invoking supervision.
    ///
    /// Uses an iterative approach with cycle detection to prevent infinite loops
    /// in case of cyclic parent relationships.
    fn handle_actor_error(&mut self, actor_id: ActorId, error: ActorError) {
        use std::collections::HashSet;

        let mut current_actor = actor_id;
        let mut current_error = error;
        let mut visited: HashSet<ActorId> = HashSet::new();
        let mut contexts_to_process: Vec<ActorContext> = Vec::new();

        loop {
            // Cycle detection
            if !visited.insert(current_actor) {
                log::error!(
                    "Cyclic supervision detected at {:?}, stopping escalation",
                    current_actor
                );
                break;
            }

            // Get the parent to supervise
            let parent_id = self.actors.get(current_actor).and_then(|e| e.parent);

            let Some(parent_id) = parent_id else {
                // No parent - log at root level
                log::error!(
                    "Unhandled actor error at root {:?}: {}",
                    current_actor,
                    current_error
                );
                break;
            };

            let mut ctx = ActorContext::new(parent_id);
            let strategy = if let Some(parent_entry) = self.actors.get_mut(parent_id) {
                parent_entry
                    .actor
                    .on_child_error(current_actor, &current_error, &mut ctx)
            } else {
                SupervisionStrategy::Escalate
            };

            contexts_to_process.push(ctx);

            match strategy {
                SupervisionStrategy::Resume => {
                    log::debug!(
                        "Supervisor {:?} resuming actor {:?}",
                        parent_id,
                        current_actor
                    );
                    break;
                }
                SupervisionStrategy::Restart => {
                    log::info!(
                        "Supervisor {:?} restarting actor {:?}",
                        parent_id,
                        current_actor
                    );
                    // For restart, we would need to store actor factory - not implemented yet
                    // For now, just resume
                    break;
                }
                SupervisionStrategy::Stop => {
                    log::info!(
                        "Supervisor {:?} stopping actor {:?}",
                        parent_id,
                        current_actor
                    );
                    self.despawn(current_actor);
                    break;
                }
                SupervisionStrategy::Escalate => {
                    log::debug!(
                        "Escalating error from {:?} to {:?}",
                        current_actor,
                        parent_id
                    );
                    current_error = ActorError::ChildError {
                        actor: current_actor,
                        error: Box::new(current_error),
                    };
                    current_actor = parent_id;
                    // Continue loop for escalation
                }
            }
        }

        // Process all collected contexts
        for ctx in contexts_to_process {
            self.process_context_requests(ctx);
        }
    }

    /// Process spawn/despawn requests from a context.
    fn process_context_requests(&mut self, mut ctx: ActorContext) {
        // Handle outgoing messages
        for msg in ctx.take_outgoing() {
            if msg.target.is_some() {
                let _ = self.send(msg);
            } else {
                let _ = self.broadcast(msg);
            }
        }

        // Handle spawn requests
        for request in ctx.take_spawn_requests() {
            let actor = (request.actor)();
            if let Some(parent) = request.parent {
                self.spawn_with_parent(actor, parent);
            } else {
                self.spawn(actor);
            }
        }

        // Handle despawn requests
        for id in ctx.take_despawn_requests() {
            self.despawn(id);
        }

        // Register inbox handles
        for (id, handle) in ctx.take_inbox_handles() {
            self.inbox_handles.insert(id, handle);
        }

        // Register handlers (with duplicate check)
        for (id, type_id) in ctx.take_handlers() {
            let handlers = self.handlers.entry(type_id).or_default();
            if !handlers.contains(&id) {
                handlers.push(id);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Get an actor by ID.
    pub fn get(&self, id: ActorId) -> Option<&dyn Actor> {
        self.actors.get(id).map(|e| e.actor.as_ref())
    }

    /// Get a mutable reference to an actor by ID.
    pub fn get_mut(&mut self, id: ActorId) -> Option<&mut Box<dyn Actor>> {
        self.actors.get_mut(id).map(|e| &mut e.actor)
    }

    /// Get the root actor.
    pub fn root(&self) -> Option<ActorId> {
        self.root
    }

    /// Get the number of actors in the registry.
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.actors.len()
    }

    /// Check if the registry is empty.
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.actors.is_empty()
    }

    /// Get an inbox handle for an actor.
    pub fn inbox(&self, id: ActorId) -> Option<InboxHandle> {
        self.inbox_handles.get(&id).cloned()
    }

    /// Get the parent of an actor.
    pub fn parent(&self, id: ActorId) -> Option<ActorId> {
        self.actors.get(id).and_then(|e| e.parent)
    }

    /// Get the children of an actor.
    pub fn children(&self, id: ActorId) -> &[ActorId] {
        self.actors
            .get(id)
            .map(|e| e.children.as_slice())
            .unwrap_or(&[])
    }

    /// Iterate over all actor IDs.
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = ActorId> + '_ {
        self.actors.keys()
    }

    /// Find actors that handle a specific message type.
    pub fn handlers_for(&self, type_id: TypeId) -> &[ActorId] {
        self.handlers
            .get(&type_id)
            .map(|v| v.as_slice())
            .unwrap_or(&[])
    }
}

impl Default for ActorRegistry {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// Thread-safe wrapper around ActorRegistry.
pub struct SharedRegistry {
    inner: RwLock<ActorRegistry>,
}

impl SharedRegistry {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            inner: RwLock::new(ActorRegistry::new()),
        }
    }

    pub fn read(&self) -> parking_lot::RwLockReadGuard<'_, ActorRegistry> {
        self.inner.read()
    }

    pub fn write(&self) -> parking_lot::RwLockWriteGuard<'_, ActorRegistry> {
        self.inner.write()
    }
}

impl Default for SharedRegistry {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    struct TestActor {
        id: ActorId,
        value: i32,
    }

    impl TestActor {
        fn new(value: i32) -> Self {
            Self {
                id: ActorId::default(),
                value,
            }
        }
    }

    impl Actor for TestActor {
        fn id(&self) -> ActorId {
            self.id
        }

        fn set_id(&mut self, id: ActorId) {
            self.id = id;
        }

        fn handles(&self) -> &[TypeId] {
            &[]
        }

        fn handle(&mut self, _msg: Message, _ctx: &mut ActorContext) -> HandleResult {
            HandleResult::NotHandled
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn spawn_and_despawn() {
        let mut registry = ActorRegistry::new();

        let id = registry.spawn(Box::new(TestActor::new(42)));
        assert_eq!(registry.len(), 1);
        assert!(registry.get(id).is_some());

        registry.despawn(id);
        assert_eq!(registry.len(), 0);
        assert!(registry.get(id).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn parent_child_relationship() {
        let mut registry = ActorRegistry::new();

        let parent_id = registry.spawn(Box::new(TestActor::new(1)));
        let child_id = registry.spawn_with_parent(Box::new(TestActor::new(2)), parent_id);

        assert_eq!(registry.parent(child_id), Some(parent_id));
        assert_eq!(registry.children(parent_id), &[child_id]);

        // Despawning parent should also despawn children
        registry.despawn(parent_id);
        assert!(registry.get(parent_id).is_none());
        assert!(registry.get(child_id).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn root_actor() {
        let mut registry = ActorRegistry::new();

        assert!(registry.root().is_none());

        let id = registry.spawn(Box::new(TestActor::new(1)));
        assert_eq!(registry.root(), Some(id));

        registry.despawn(id);
        assert!(registry.root().is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn metrics_tracking() {
        let mut registry = ActorRegistry::new();

        let id = registry.spawn(Box::new(TestActor::new(1)));
        let metrics = registry.metrics().snapshot();
        assert_eq!(metrics.actors_spawned, 1);

        registry.despawn(id);
        let metrics = registry.metrics().snapshot();
        assert_eq!(metrics.actors_despawned, 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn broadcast_delivers_to_handlers() {
        use std::any::TypeId;

        struct BroadcastHandler {
            id: ActorId,
            handles: Vec<TypeId>,
            received: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool,
        }

        struct TestMessage(i32);

        impl BroadcastHandler {
            fn new() -> Self {
                Self {
                    id: ActorId::default(),
                    handles: vec![TypeId::of::<TestMessage>()],
                    received: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
                }
            }
        }

        impl Actor for BroadcastHandler {
            fn id(&self) -> ActorId {
                self.id
            }

            fn set_id(&mut self, id: ActorId) {
                self.id = id;
            }

            fn handles(&self) -> &[TypeId] {
                &self.handles
            }

            fn handle(&mut self, msg: Message, _ctx: &mut ActorContext) -> HandleResult {
                if msg.is::<TestMessage>() {
                    self.received.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
                    HandleResult::Handled
                } else {
                    HandleResult::NotHandled
                }
            }
        }

        let mut registry = ActorRegistry::new();

        // Spawn a sender
        let sender_id = registry.spawn(Box::new(TestActor::new(0)));

        // Spawn handlers
        let _handler1_id = registry.spawn(Box::new(BroadcastHandler::new()));
        let _handler2_id = registry.spawn(Box::new(BroadcastHandler::new()));

        // Broadcast a message
        let msg = Message::broadcast(TestMessage(42), sender_id);
        let delivered = registry.broadcast(msg);

        // Both handlers should have received the message
        assert_eq!(delivered, 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn no_duplicate_handlers() {
        use std::any::TypeId;

        struct HandlerActor {
            id: ActorId,
            handles: Vec<TypeId>,
        }

        struct TestMessage;

        impl Actor for HandlerActor {
            fn id(&self) -> ActorId {
                self.id
            }

            fn set_id(&mut self, id: ActorId) {
                self.id = id;
            }

            fn handles(&self) -> &[TypeId] {
                &self.handles
            }

            fn handle(&mut self, _msg: Message, _ctx: &mut ActorContext) -> HandleResult {
                HandleResult::Handled
            }
        }

        let mut registry = ActorRegistry::new();

        let id = registry.spawn(Box::new(HandlerActor {
            id: ActorId::default(),
            handles: vec![TypeId::of::<TestMessage>()],
        }));

        // Try to register the same handler again via context
        let mut ctx = ActorContext::new(id);
        ctx.register_handler(id, TypeId::of::<TestMessage>());
        registry.process_context_requests(ctx);

        // Should still only have one handler
        let handlers = registry.handlers_for(TypeId::of::<TestMessage>());
        assert_eq!(handlers.len(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn deep_actor_hierarchy_despawn() {
        // Test that deep hierarchies don't cause stack overflow (uses iterative despawn)
        let mut registry = ActorRegistry::new();

        // Create a chain of parent -> child -> grandchild etc.
        let root = registry.spawn(Box::new(TestActor::new(0)));
        let mut current = root;

        // Create 100 levels of nesting
        for i in 1..=100 {
            let child = registry.spawn_with_parent(Box::new(TestActor::new(i)), current);
            current = child;
        }

        assert_eq!(registry.len(), 101);

        // Despawn root should despawn all 101 actors
        registry.despawn(root);

        assert_eq!(registry.len(), 0);
        let metrics = registry.metrics().snapshot();
        assert_eq!(metrics.actors_despawned, 101);
    }

    #[test]
    fn send_result_types() {
        let mut registry = ActorRegistry::new();
        let actor_id = registry.spawn(Box::new(TestActor::new(1)));

        // Create a message to a non-existent actor
        let mut actors: slotmap::SlotMap<ActorId, ()> = slotmap::SlotMap::with_key();
        let fake_source = actors.insert(());
        let fake_target = actors.insert(());

        let msg = Message::new(fake_target, 42i32, fake_source);
        let result = registry.send(msg);

        // Should be ActorNotFound
        assert!(matches!(result, SendResult::ActorNotFound(_)));

        // Cleanup
        registry.despawn(actor_id);
    }
}
